description: A macro whose result is a literal is rejected: 'defmacro one() do quote do: 1 end' fails with 'lower/unsupported: macro N returned non-source value 1' (compiler2/world.rs, the match on the macro's returned value after run_macro_on_source). In Elixir a literal (atom, number, binary, list, 2-tuple) is valid quoted code: defmacro one(), do: quote(do: 1) and defmacro two(), do: 2 return 1 and 2 (verified with the elixir CLI). Fix: the macro result path accepts every quoted-literal shape and turns it into source, using the same literal encoding the quoted source tree already has. Done when: a fixture where macros return quote do: 1, a bare 2, an atom and a 2-tuple asserts each value, and fails first. One commit.
title: A macro may return a bare literal, as in Elixir
